sec: PCT bicarbonate reabsorption: the CA IV / CA II diagram · p821

items.q: In the PCT diagram, which transporter sits on the luminal membrane of the proximal tubule cell?
items.exp: The luminal membrane carries the Na⁺–H⁺ exchanger; the basolateral membrane carries the Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger. (Book p821)

items.q: Step ① of the PCT diagram — the hydration/dehydration of carbonic acid in the lumen — is catalysed by:
opts: No enzyme — the step is spontaneous
items.exp: Step ① is luminal carbonic anhydrase IV acting on HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂CO₃; step ③ is cytoplasmic CA II. (Book p821)

items.q: Step ③ inside the PCT cell, generating H₂CO₃ from CO₂ and H₂O, is catalysed by:
items.exp: Cytoplasmic carbonic anhydrase II (CA II) hydrates CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ inside the cell; the luminal enzyme is CA IV. (Book p821)

items.q: Match the numbered PCT steps — 1) Step ①  2) Step ②  3) Step ③  4) Step ④ … A) Dissociation of H₂CO₃ into H⁺ and HCO₃⁻  B) CA IV acting on HCO₃⁻ and H⁺  C) CA II forming H₂CO₃ from CO₂ and H₂O  D) Splitting of H₂CO₃ into H₂O and CO₂
items.exp: Luminal CA IV forms H₂CO₃ (①), which splits to H₂O + CO₂ (②); CO₂ enters the cell and CA II rebuilds H₂CO₃ (③), which dissociates to H⁺ and HCO₃⁻ (④). (Book p821)

items.q: How does the HCO₃⁻ formed inside the PCT cell leave for the blood side?
opts: By simple diffusion across the luminal membrane
items.exp: The regenerated HCO₃⁻ exits across the basolateral membrane on the Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger, while H⁺ leaves apically on the Na⁺–H⁺ exchanger. (Book p821)

items.q: Match the arrows entering the PCT cell from the lumen — 1) H₂O  2) Na⁺  3) Ca²⁺ … A) Reabsorbed cation named third  B) Reabsorbed cation named second  C) Reabsorbed with the filtrate solvent
items.exp: The diagram shows H₂O, Na⁺ and Ca²⁺ reabsorbed from lumen into the PCT cell along with CO₂. (Book p821)

items.q: Fill up: In the PCT diagram, CA stands for ______.
items.exp: CA = carbonic anhydrase, the enzyme family catalysing the luminal (CA IV) and cytoplasmic (CA II) steps. (Book p821)

items.q: Acetazolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase in the PCT. Predict the effect from the printed diagram.
opts: Both the luminal CA IV and cytoplasmic CA II steps fail, so HCO₃⁻ reabsorption falls
Only the basolateral Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger is inhibited
HCO₃⁻ reabsorption increases because H₂CO₃ accumulates
Only the Na⁺–H⁺ exchanger is inhibited, sparing HCO₃⁻
items.exp: The diagram places CA IV luminally (step ①) and CA II in the cytoplasm (step ③); blocking carbonic anhydrase breaks both steps of HCO₃⁻ reabsorption. (Book p821)

items.q: All but one of these are shown moving across the luminal border of the PCT cell in the diagram. Which is the odd one out?
opts: HCO₃⁻ moving from blood into the lumen
items.exp: The diagram shows Na⁺, CO₂ and H₂O entering the cell and H⁺ leaving into the lumen; HCO₃⁻ movement is basolateral, into the blood. (Book p821)
